caveats: Current latest update timestamps count distinct records by their latest update only; they do not reconstruct all updates made during historical periods.
Current stage and latest stage-change timestamp do not reconstruct stage movement history or demonstrate forward progression.
Call due dates describe scheduled activity dates, not booking creation dates. Marked done describes CRM completion, not independent proof a call was held.

Sales Pipeline values exclude Leads/Referral pipelines and nurture/graveyard stages. Values are source-entered and valuation basis is unverified; they are not recognized revenue or verified qualified pipeline.
Won/lost dates are the current retained timestamps; reopened/re-won deal history is not reconstructed.
Pipedrive timestamps lacking an explicit offset are interpreted as UTC; date-only due dates are retained unchanged.
Scope is all accessible, non-deleted deals and accessible done/undone activities. Deleted records are excluded; account permissions may restrict visibility.
Obvious test-labelled deals and activities are retained in the record inventory but excluded from all business summaries.
All current open deal values are zero. Show pipeline valuation as unpopulated rather than claiming the commercial pipeline is worth zero.
Open status can coexist with Closed Won/Closed Lost stage labels; stage labels are not substitutes for actual won/lost status.
Collection is a paginated snapshot, not an atomic database transaction; records can change during collection.

Structured history is retained for a defined 44-deal subset since September 1. These observed changes are not account-wide progression, and Closed Won stage entry is not won status or verified revenue.

Is the Rule of 40 still relevant for SaaS #founders?

While companies that achieve it often command premium exit multiples (10.5x vs. ~6x EV/Revenue), the reality is that most public SaaS businesses fall well short of this benchmark. 

In this post, we explore:

✅  What the Rule of 40 is and represents
✅  How many companies actually meet the threshold
✅  Whether it remains a meaningful metric in today’s market

We also examine how founders should think about the Rule of 40 based on stage -- and when it’s most strategic to use it as a performance signal versus a guiding principle.

📌 Additional resources for founders are included at the end 📌 

#RuleOf40 #SaaSFounders #StartupMetrics #CapitalEfficiency #Fundraising #VCReadiness #B2BStartups #FounderInsights #B2BSaaS #FractionalCFO #CentripetalAdvisors

In this video, Megadata Health Systems CEO Shalom Reinman shares his experience partnering with the Centripetal Advisors team. 

Together, we:
 ✅ Raised $12.5M in debt and equity with top-tier backers (TIMIA Capital, Avidbank, Blueprint Equity, Channel Equity Partners, Blossom Street Ventures )
 ✅ Built a SaaS-native financial infrastructure, board reporting, and KPI frameworks
 ✅ Offloaded financial operations from the founder—freeing him to focus on growth
✅ Took a board seat and invested directly in the company

💡 Founders: if its unclear how your finance function is actually helping you scale, watch the video to hear how the right partner can make all the difference.

From our founder, Charles Solomon. When it comes to fundraising (in the immortal words of Montell Jordan) This Is How We Do It!
🚀  $16M Closed in Q1. Zero Term Sheets to Done Deals in 54 Days. 👏

From our conversations with LP-backed Series A investors and funds still deploying, the message is crystal clear: 

in 2025, capital flows will bifurcate.

Some of it will chase AI-driven breakout potential....

The rest? 
It’s going to highly disciplined, well-prepared companies that know their numbers cold—not just those with a good story.

❗The middle—companies that are “fine but fuzzy”—will be ignored.

Here’s what we’re seeing:

-⏱️ Deal cycles are getting longer.
-🔍 Diligence standards are higher.
-📉 Valuations are softening—unless you're in the top decile of metrics.
-💡 Operational discipline = capital optionality.
-🧩 M&A is back on the table as a way to grow smarter in a tighter market.
--------------------------------------------
So what does this mean for founders? You must know:

- How do you benchmark against your peers?
- Can you tell the capital story that fits your stage, risk profile, and growth ambitions?
- Is your strategy built for this market—or the one you wish you were in?

If you don’t have sharp answers, you need sharper partners.

At Centripetal Advisors, we help B2B founders build the financial strategy, investor materials, and operating discipline needed to command capital—debt or equity. And in a world where mediocrity is being re-priced, that edge is everything.

Let’s talk about your capital strategy:

notes: A Calendly booking verifies platform scheduling only. Generic 30-minute types are unclassified; they may include partners, recruiting or other non-sales conversations.
Interview event types are kept for source reconciliation and excluded from business-call indicators until purpose is reviewed.
Two lifecycle concepts remain separate: bookingCreatedAt is the original reschedule-chain creation date; startAt is the scheduled occurrence date.
Canceled original events and replacement events are linked by bookingChainId. Count unique chains for booking creation, and only isCurrentBooking records for upcoming active bookings.
An active event in the past is not attendance evidence. No-show absence, elapsed end time and CRM marked-done activity do not independently verify that a call was held.
Exact name and email matches corroborate identity only. They do not establish channel attribution, qualified status, opportunity acceptance or revenue.
